notes: Hebrew has two כְּ phrases; the ASV makes the second the English subject, so only the first preposition has an English word (*even as*) and the second is unrepresented under rule 22.
The relational *of* goes to the participle as nomen rectum, the unit discontinuous around the article's *him that* (rules 19, 25, 41); the competing reading attaches the *of* to the article's unit.
*unto him* is `added`: the Hebrew participle writes no object, so neither the preposition nor the pronoun answers to a morpheme (rules 30, 44); the starring corroborates without deciding (rule 7).
